version_guard.provenance: All four guarded probes ran against concrete Claude Code 2.1.296 on 2026-10-09; each ended version-guard: verdict=single-version start=2.1.296 end=2.1.296. Arm S observed concurrent hook execution in 12/12 event pairs with relay-first in 4/12; Arm D verified an errored Bash tool result in each of five denied runs and one Stop per run; Arm T killed all eight overrun firings while all four sessions exited 0 with replies, at a mean 5.2 s (range 5.0–5.3 s). The dedicated TUI probe observed one Stop per turn at 1.5 s / 1.2 s. Arm P was rerun with --dangerously-skip-permissions after an allowed-tools-only attempt was blocked by the auto-mode classifier; the completed print-mode run performed both sequential tool rounds and fired one Stop. One authenticated claude-print stream-json PTY capture used the same pinned binary; its 41-record stdout was byte-identical to the transcript, with no result, CR, or blank records. The sanitized golden representatives include wireToolInputs, permissionDecision, and a thinking block; replay bytes and error objects were generated through the production reader and emitter.

notes.isolation: Every probe ran with HOME redirected into a throwaway sandbox; the host real settings and .claude.json were not read or modified. The host credentials file, when present, was copied file-to-file into the sandbox and never printed.
notes.cross_source_order_evidence: 2.1.296 Arm S: project hook sleeping 300 ms and relay hook 0 ms ran concurrently in 12/12 event pairs; the relay started first in 4/12. The result is concurrency, not a contractual source order: claude-print must not depend on which hook starts first.
notes.tui_per_turn_evidence: The dedicated probe-tui-second-turn.sh run on 2.1.296 completed two TUI turns: turn 1 fired 1 Stop with its reply rendered in 1.5 s, and turn 2 fired 1 Stop with SECOND-OK rendered in 1.2 s. The allowed-tool probe completed one Stop per turn (51.0 s and 29.0 s); those timings are separate from the dedicated plain-turn probe.
notes.degraded_path_hazard: Arm D on 2.1.296 used a command-specific Bash deny rule and verified an errored Bash tool result in each transcript. All 5 completed denied runs exited 0 and fired exactly one Stop. The historical 2.1.270 extra-Stop hazard did not reproduce. The poller keeps first-payload tolerance for degraded runs.
notes.print_mode_tool_use_evidence: Arm P on 2.1.296 used --dangerously-skip-permissions in the isolated probe project after the allowed-tools-only attempt was blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier. Both sequential Bash rounds completed in order, the final message was DONE, exit was 0, and exactly 1 Stop fired.
notes.cutoff_evidence: The focused 2.1.296 -p run with --max-turns 2 exited 1 and logged zero new Stop firings; the cutoff remains owned by the --stop-hook-timeout watchdog, not the Stop Poller.
notes.hook_timeout_evidence: Arm T on 2.1.296 configured a relay-position hook with timeout 5 s and sleep 30 s: all 8 event firings were killed, all 4 sessions exited 0 with replies rendered, and Stop hook-to-process completion averaged 5.2 s (range 5.0–5.3 s). This confirms the per-hook timeout field used by the relay.
